Occurrences.Kwic: 師云：聞底事作麼生？進云：非唯觀世音，我亦從中證。師云：有眼如盲猶似可，有耳如聾笑殺人。進云：只如釋迦已滅，彌勒未生，正當與麼時，佛法如何舉論？師云：盡在法昌拄杖頭。進云：學人為什麼不曉？師云：杲日當天，盲人摸地。進云：與麼則大眾沾恩去也。師云：你見箇什麼道理？進云：欲言言不及，林下好商量。師云：亂統禪和，如麻似粟。僧問：世尊出世，先度五俱輪；和尚出世，先度何人？師云：隨泥作佛。進云：學人正在迷途，和尚為什麼不垂方便？師拈起拄杖云：見麼？進云：見。師云：莫道無方便。進云：莫便是和尚為人處也無？師放下拄杖，僧禮拜。師云：邯鄲學唐步。僧問：祖意西來即不問，陞堂演法事如何？師云：家常茶飯。進云：與麼則勞而無功去也。

Senses.Explanation: As thick as hemp and millet. Fachang Yiyu, pressed at the end of a question round — the dharma all on his staff's tip, the blind man groping under the noon sun — dismisses the questioner's polite retreat with the verdict: disorderly Chan-wanderers, thick as hemp and millet. Dahui Zonggao, seated for Minister Zhang while a monk announces the selection-ground for buddhas and the empty-mind graduation, answers with the cooked-up variant — cooked-up Chan-wanderers, thick as hemp and millet — before grading the candidate's examiner ambition three hundred sixty years off. Xuedou Chongxian, appraising the two elders of the Wuzhou-ridge meeting in the Classified Anthology — one only releases, one only holds — waits a long beat, then rules: board-carrying Chan-wanderers, thick as hemp and millet. And Zhantang Wenzhun, finding his young student reading the Diamond Sutra and testing him on the dharma's evenness against Yunju's height and Baofeng's lowness, drops the same brand on the answer and walks out — the student, standing behind, secretly delighted that an eyed teacher knows he is already on the right road. Gulin Qingmao, after a visiting monk performs his one-word-severs-a-thousand-rivers flourish without a word of his own, brands the shape: disorderly Chan-wanderers, thick as hemp and millet. Liangting Jingting, defending sutra study against the throw-away-everything crowd, counts them off — cooked-up elders, thick as hemp and millet, who read no sutras, practice no deportment, call it the shortcut, and set up shop as village gate-masters with a few memorized set pieces. Chaozong Tongren, dismantling a student's gloss on Hanyue's broken root-tail, asks the counterfactual: when Dahui and Ying'an came forth, those teaching in every quarter were thick as hemp and millet — can it be they had no insight at all? So why could none of them handle it? And Hanyue Fazang, drumming on an awning of void with sun and moon for drumsticks to summon five hundred wooden arhats from Deng Mountain to haul firewood and steam millet on Rice-Hoard Peak, inverts the measure — the three-times buddhas themselves thick as hemp and millet, applauding in empty space, with only Samantabhadra's eldest son riding the reclining-elephant peak as witness.
